confidence_notes: Medium. Meal, beer and cappuccino anchors rest on Numbeo-derived San Sebastian figures republished by third-party sites (Expatica, Expatistan, MyLifeElsewhere). I saw them only as web-search summaries and did not open the pages. Travel-guide ranges also informed them. Numbeo-style averages probably lag July tourist-season prices, so I nudged the mid-range meal and coffee up slightly. Cocktail and wine are the weakest food and drink anchors. Guides and blogs give roughly EUR 8-12 for a gin and tonic or cocktail and EUR 2.50-4 for a glass of wine at pintxo bars. I therefore used the local beer relationship: cocktail about 2.5x beer, restaurant wine glass about equal to beer. Accommodation is a holistic July high-season estimate from general knowledge. I checked no listings or booking pages, and festival periods (Jazzaldia, Semana Grande) can run well above it. EUR prices were converted to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.16 USD per EUR from general knowledge, which I did not search.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based mainly on San Sebastian's own aggregated figures. Search summaries put the city roughly 11-17% above the Spanish average on cost-of-living indexes. Accommodation and cocktail levels are benchmarked from general knowledge against premium Spanish tourist cities such as Barcelona in high season. The pintxo-bar culture keeps beer, wine and coffee near Spanish norms, while sit-down restaurant meals and lodging are at the upper end of Spain.
